table: composition (K-P9-6: atx-equity-strategy-ic --list-rules --json, block theme_schedule shared with theme-tsmom-v1, stage schedule)
citation: Barroso and Santa-Clara (2015), Momentum has its moments, Journal of Financial Economics 116(1), 111-120 (lit [18]); real-time form: Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang and Yan (2020), On the performance of volatility-managed portfolios, Journal of Financial Economics 138(1), 95-117 (lit [17]); Daniel and Moskowitz (2016), Momentum crashes, Journal of Financial Economics 122(2) (lit [19])
claim: momentum's own realised volatility forecasts its next-month volatility but not its mean, so scaling WML to a constant volatility by its six-month realised volatility lifts its Sharpe from .53 to .97 (BSC); volatility management fails in real time for about half of 103 strategies, momentum among the exceptions (Cederburg et al.; lit section 1.6)
source_sample_basis: the rule's real-time form is Cederburg et al.'s, whose samples 'end in December 2016' (read on 2026-10-03 in the text of lit [17]'s URL); the hypothesis's own source, Barroso and Santa-Clara, ends 2011:12 (sample 1927:03 - 2011:12); the later end is registered because it is the last published sample in which the registered real-time form was tested; both lie before the house window
predicted_mechanism: the momentum sleeve's volatility clusters and is unrelated to its next-month mean, so holding the price_momentum theme's mass inversely to its trailing six-month realised volatility, against the running mean of those estimates, cuts momentum-crash variance at about the same momentum return
house_form: the price_momentum theme's mass in the composition, W_pm x target_b / sigma_b per block, as a theme_schedule rule beside theme-tsmom-v1 (lit section 6 row 7: 'add a vol-schedule rule there'; atx-impl strategy_ic_mom_volman.cpp; the fitter records the sleeve as theme-tsmom-v1's step 1 forms it, composition_mom_volman.py)

constants.name: lookback
constants.why: Barroso and Santa-Clara's six months of daily returns (their sigma-hat is the realised variance of the preceding 126 daily WML returns, squared returns without a mean)

constants.name: lag
constants.why: the house's decision -> fill -> return clock: the sleeve's value at decision d is realised at d + 2, so block j reads only d <= j - 2

constants.name: step
constants.why: one month of decisions: BSC rebalance monthly; the house's monthly step (theme-tsmom-v1's)

constants.name: target
constants.value: running mean of the sleeve's own estimates sigma_0 .. sigma_b
constants.why: Cederburg et al.'s real-time constant: BSC's full-sample target is look-ahead; the running mean uses only estimates known at the block

constants.name: cap
constants.why: BSC scale without a cap; a cap would be a second constant with no published value (stated as a concern in the lane report: a low-volatility block can scale the momentum mass up without bound)

fixed_choices: only the price_momentum theme's mass moves; every other theme keeps the parent's W_t
the sleeve is theme-tsmom-v1's step-1 sleeve of the price_momentum theme over the parent fit's role decisions (sum over its members of (w_k / W_t) s_k f_k(d), flat 0, 0 outside the TRAIN mask)
block b starts at decision 127 + 21 b; before the first block the parent's masses; the masses ride the theme schedule theme-tsmom-v1 uses, so the two schedules exclude each other
a block whose scale target / sigma is not finite is refused with the rule's name (no cap: a tiny positive sigma gives a large finite scale, accepted; review S-1, Ruling ALCOMB-4)
the schedule is fixed on the fit's TRAIN sleeve (Ruling ALCOMB-4): a role outside those sessions keeps the parent's masses before the first recorded block and the last block's after it

the sleeve is recorded by the fitter's Python pass on the final weights; --engine-fit is refused with --mom-volman (the C++ composition fit records no momentum sleeve; lane D3 adds it, Ruling ALCOMB-7; each P9 cell uses the fit mode of its P9-B0 parent reference)
the IC exe prints sigma_b, target_b and scale_b per block in each scored role's summary entry (composition_schedule_trace; Ruling ALCOMB-5, review S-3)

predictions.registered_before_any_read: the momentum sleeve's realised volatility falls and its Sharpe rises after scaling (plan section 5.2 P9-M prints both); book effect small: price_momentum holds about .057 of the weight after ERC (lit section 1.6)
